full_judgment: 7. The contention of Mr. Moqbul Ahmed that the court below acted in excess of their jurisdiction in making the order that the petitioner is to repay the entire money due to the complainant opposite party has got substance. Mr. Abdul Momen Chowdhury very candidly submitted that the court has no such power and he is unable to support this part of the order passed by the court below. A criminal court while awarding punishment under section 406 of the Penal Code has got no authority to pass an order directing the accused to pay the entire sale proceeds of the property entrusted with him or over which he had dominion to the complainant. Section 406 of the Penal Code 'speaks of awarding punishment by a court with imprisonment of either description or with fine or both. It does not empower a criminal court to pass an order directing the accused to pay the sale proceeds of a property to the complainant in respect of which the charge of criminal breach of trust is established against the accused. From a perusal of the judgment of both the courts below it appears that they did not impose any fine on the accused petitioner in terms of section 406 of the Penal Code but the direction for payment for the money given by the trial and affirmed by the lower appellate court seems to me to be in the nature of decree of a civil court which can be given in a properly constituted Money Suit or suit for damage or suit for similar nature. Therefore, in my opinion, the courts below in passing the order to repay the sale proceeds to the complainant transgressed its jurisdiction and acted ex mero motu. As the court acted in making such order beyond its province the order is liable to be set aside. Accordingly, it is set aside. But the order of the lower appellate court so far as it relates to conviction and sentence it is hereby maintained.
